sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r7/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 15 (#14), Internal Quality Checks row 15 (#14 annotation: flag credentials in task data; only toml allowed), Deterministic Checks check-fixtures.py and check-probe-not-in-seed.py rows
evidence: Parsed the only shipped data file, .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r7/task/environment/assets/seed_data.json (SHA256 a1c65c80...e83740, byte-identical to solution/app/src/seed_data.json and to the hash recorded in raw-evidence-index.json), with an in-memory Python script. Results: 10 users, 3 jobs, 16 applications, 127 messages, 3 notes, 6 read markers; no duplicate ids or user emails. Reference integrity: every job recruiter_id/manager_id resolves to a user with role recruiter/hiring_manager; every application job_id resolves and its stage is in stages; positions are contiguous 1..n for every (job, stage); no duplicate (job, lower(email)); every candidate email matches the address pattern; the 3 candidate accounts' emails map to applications whose candidate_name equals the account name (Noor -> APP-101, APP-302; Tomas -> APP-201; Lena -> APP-301). Only APP-301 is REJECTED and it carries rejected_from=SCREEN (non-Hired) and a non-blank reason; no other row carries rejection fields. Interview counts are within limits (PLAT 2/3, DATA 1/2, DSGN 1/3). Every message's application_id and sender_id resolve and the sender is allowed in that conversation under hireops_rules.md section 6 (recruiters anywhere; candidates only their own); bodies non-blank; timestamps strictly increasing per conversation (APP-101 120, APP-201 3, APP-301 3, APP-302 1). Every note author is a recruiter or that job's manager (MGR1 on APP-101/JOB-PLAT, MGR3 on APP-301/JOB-DSGN), matching section 3 Internal notes. Every read marker is unique per (user, application), is held by a participant, and is 0 <= read_count <= message count; derived unread: Lena 1, Mei Lin 2, others 0. Agreement with public text and graders: stages and candidate_status_labels equal the table in hireops_rules.md:183-190; thread_page_size 30 matches :144 and :209; seed note in rules :204-209 (three jobs, one long conversation, read markers counted from the first) matches; app_context.md:29-30 '120 messages' matches; functional prompt.md:25 / judge.toml:335 'Lena starts with 1 unread' matches derived value; judge.toml:407 Platform order Applied Greta, Ade, Marco and Screen Priya, Samuel matches positions; Noor's note text matches notes[0]. Clean/synthetic: all emails use RFC 2606 reserved .example domains (hireops.example, candidates.example, mail.example); no phone numbers, addresses, DOBs, ids or real contact data; no password, token, key or URL anywhere in the seed (the shared demo password appears only in instruction.md:17 and rules:11, which the skill profile and Internal Quality Checks annotation for row 14 permit). Scan for <, >, script, javascript:, ${, {{, 'ignore', 'judge', 'score', http found nothing; all ASCII. The only 'instruction' hit is generated_note pointing to /instructions/hireops_rules.md, an informational pointer, not an imperative to graders. Weak/alternative app probes: a conforming app that advances a sender's marker to cover their own sent message (CAN1 #120, REC3 #3 sit after their markers) sees identical unread and seen results because own messages are never unread (rules:152-153) and seen depends on the other party's marker; so no conforming reading diverges from grader expectations. A seed-copy/static app gains nothing from the seed here because the gated rows require new jobs/cards. Minor, non-defect observations: (1) read markers of 119 (CAN1) and 2 (REC3) lag their own last sent message, harmless as above; (2) narrative tension: APP-301 is rejected from SCREEN yet REC3's 2026-07-29 message says 'We will write again once the panel has met'; no rejection timestamp is seeded, so it is not a contradiction. Neither affects grading. Evidence type: static source parse only; this row needs no runtime measurement. I did not run the private check-fixtures.py checker.
